title: Dharana
description: Develop the power of single-pointed concentration, the essential precursor to meditation and the key to mental clarity.

sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas

sutra.sanskrit:
त॒तः॒ क्षी॒य॒ते प्रकाशा॑वर॒णम्
धा॒र॒णासु च योग्यता॑ मन॒सः
sutra.meaning: From that is dissipated, the mental darkness which veils the light, ... and from that, is attained the state of the mind for linking the attention to a higher concentration force or person.

sections.insight: Pranayama removes the veil covering the light of knowledge and heralds the dawn of wisdom. The mind becomes fit, thereafter, for Dharana or concentration.. the next limb of yoga.Once the mind is still and free of thought it can focus on a single point. This is when it can manifest what it wants.
sections.practice: Make a commitment and effort to intensify your practice. Meditate for 20 min

sutra.meaning: Fixing the consciousness on one point or region is Dharana.

sections.insight: The yogi must be so familiar with the realm of his mind and emotions, that he should begin to recognize where the thoughts, ideas, images and memories are arising. . Then he can practice the sixth stage of yoga, which is putting his attention to a single object or region.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my mind quiet enough to permit me to focus on a single object for a significant duration of my meditation.
sections.practice: Practice focusing on a part of your body, say the heart with eyes closed.

sutra.meaning: Focused awareness on one object stabilizes the mind

sections.reflectionPrompt: Bring your attention to your breath
sections.practice: Observe breathing for as long as it takes to go into meditation.

sutra.meaning: Meditate on an object of your choice which is spiritually uplifting to you

sections.practice: Meditate at a chosen spot on a chosen idea or object.

sutra.meaning: Mastery extends from smallest to largest

sections.practice: Observe deeply everything you see today.

sutra.meaning: The seer the seen and the instrument of perception become one.When mind becomes clear it reflects reality like a crystal

sections.insight: When the mind is pure it reflects truth without distortion.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my perception clear or colored?
